summary: Four kinds of people still need to bring a korban before they may eat holy food. Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov adds a ger and a nazir.

chunks.en: There are four who are "missing atonement," and four
chunks.st: There are four individuals whose halakhic status is defined as: Lacking atonement [khappara],
chunks.stMore: which means they had been in a state of ritual impurity and underwent rituals to purify themselves, but since they have not yet brought the requisite atonement offering to complete the purification process, they may not partake of sacrificial meat.

chunks.en: who bring a korban for sinning on purpose just as for sinning by mistake.
chunks.st: And there are also four individuals who bring an offering for an intentional transgression in the same manner as they do for an unwitting transgression.

chunks.en: These are the ones missing atonement:
chunks.st: And these are the four individuals who lack atonement:

chunks.en: a zav, a zavah,
chunks.st: The man who experiences a gonorrhea-like discharge [zav], the woman who experiences a discharge of uterine blood after her menstrual period [zava],

words.note: A man with a kind of tumah that comes from his body.
A woman with a kind of tumah that comes from her body.

chunks.en: a woman who had a baby, and a metzora.
chunks.st: the woman after childbirth, and the leper.
chunks.stMore: In all four of these cases, although the individual has completed all of the other steps of the purification process, the process is not complete until the atonement offering has been brought.

words.en: and the woman who had a baby

words.note: A person with tzaraas, a skin sickness sent as a punishment.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says:

chunks.he: גֵּר, מְחֻסַּר כַּפָּרָה עַד שֶׁיִּזָּרֵק עָלָיו הַדָּם.
chunks.en: a ger is missing atonement until the blood of his korban is sprinkled for him,
chunks.st: A convert also lacks atonement, even after he has been circumcised and has immersed in a ritual bath, until the priest sprinkles the blood of his offering on the altar on his behalf.

chunks.en: and a nazir, for his wine, his haircut, and his tumah.
chunks.st: A nazirite also lacks atonement with regard to his permission for drinking wine, and cutting his hair, and his exposure to ritual impurity imparted by a corpse, until his offerings are sacrificed.

summary: Here are four people who bring the same korban whether they sinned on purpose or by mistake.

chunks.en: These bring a korban for sinning on purpose just as for sinning by mistake:
chunks.st: These individuals bring an offering for an intentional transgression in the same manner as they do for an unwitting transgression:

chunks.en: One who sins with the shifchah,
chunks.st: One who engages in intercourse with an espoused maidservant, who is liable to bring a guilt offering (see Leviticus 19:20–22);

words.note: A maidservant who is promised to be married to a Jewish slave.

chunks.en: and a nazir who became tamei,
chunks.st: and a nazirite who became ritually impure, who is required to bring a sheep as a guilt offering and two doves or two pigeons, one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering (see Numbers 6:9–12);

chunks.en: and one who falsely swears he knows no testimony,
chunks.st: and one who falsely takes the oath of testimony, asserting that he does not have any testimony to provide on a given issue (see Leviticus 5:1);

chunks.en: and one who falsely swears about something left with him.
chunks.st: and one who falsely takes the oath on a deposit, asserting that an item belonging to another is not in his possession (see Leviticus 5:21–26).

words.note: Something that someone gave him to watch.

summary: Some people bring only one korban even though they sinned many times. Others bring a korban oleh v'yored. This mishnah begins listing the first group.

chunks.en: Five people bring one korban
chunks.st: There are five individuals who bring one offering

chunks.en: for many sins,
chunks.st: for several transgressions,
chunks.stMore: i.e., for violating the same transgression several times;

chunks.en: and five bring a korban oleh v'yored.
chunks.st: and there are five individuals who bring a sliding-scale offering,
chunks.stMore: which is determined based on the financial status of the sinner.

words.note: A korban that goes up and down: a rich person brings more, a poor person less.

chunks.en: These bring one korban
chunks.st: These are the five individuals who bring one offering

chunks.en: for many sins:
chunks.st: for several transgressions:

chunks.en: One who sins with the shifchah many times,
chunks.st: First, one who engages in several acts of intercourse with an espoused maidservant,

chunks.en: and a nazir who became tamei many times,
chunks.st: and second, a nazirite who became ritually impure due to several instances of contact with ritual impurity.
chunks.stMore: The mishna continues to list the five situations in which one offering is brought to atone for several transgressions:

chunks.he: וְהַמְקַנֵּא לְאִשְׁתּוֹ עַל יְדֵי אֲנָשִׁים הַרְבֵּה,
chunks.en: and one who warns his wife about many men,
chunks.explain: He warned her not to be alone with them.
chunks.st: Third, one who issues a warning to his wife declaring himself jealous with regard to several different men
chunks.stMore: with whom he suspects her of committing adultery, and forbidding her to be alone with them. If the wife was then found separately in seclusion with each of the men, he brings her to the Temple with one single meal offering of jealousy.

chunks.en: and a metzora who got tzaraas many times.
chunks.st: And fourth, a leper who was afflicted with several instances of leprosy,
chunks.stMore: meaning that he was purified from his leprosy, and before he brought his offerings, he suffered a relapse of the leprosy. When he is finally purified, he brings only one set of offerings.

chunks.en: If he brought his birds and then got tzaraas again,
chunks.st: If a leper brought the two requisite birds on the first day of his purification (see Leviticus 14:4–7), and prior to bringing his offerings on the eighth day of his purification he was afflicted with a relapse of leprosy,

chunks.en: they do not count for him
chunks.st: those birds do not satisfy his obligation

chunks.en: until he brings his chatas.
chunks.st: until he brings his sin offering.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: until he brings his asham.
chunks.st: Until he brings his guilt offering.

summary: This mishnah finishes the list of people who bring one korban for many times, and lists who brings a korban oleh v'yored. Then it explains how the shifchah is different from other forbidden relationships.
stIntro: The mishna continues with the last of the five situations in which one offering is brought to atone for several transgressions:

chunks.en: A woman who had many babies,
chunks.st: A woman who gave birth to several offspring.
chunks.stMore: This is a case where a woman gave birth to a daughter, after which she is ritually impure for fourteen days and then enters a period of sixty-six days of ritual purity, even if she experiences uterine bleeding. Nevertheless, during this interim period, she is still somewhat impure, and it is therefore prohibited for her to enter the Temple or to partake of consecrated food, and at the end of the period she must bring an offering.

chunks.en: or lost a girl pregnancy within eighty days, and again
chunks.st: And during those days of ritual purity, she became pregnant again and then miscarried a female fetus within the eighty days, and then

chunks.en: lost a girl pregnancy within eighty days,
chunks.st: became pregnant again and miscarried another female fetus within eighty days of the first miscarriage.
chunks.stMore: In this situation, when she ultimately completes her process of purification, she brings one single offering for all the births and miscarriages.

chunks.en: or a woman who lost twins.
chunks.st: And a similar halakha applies to a woman who miscarries multiple fetuses
chunks.stMore: from a single pregnancy at different points in time, miscarrying each fetus before completing the purification period of forty days for a male or eighty days for a female for the previous fetus. When she finally completes her process of purification, she brings one single offering for all of the miscarriages.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.stMore: In these cases, a single offering does not suffice for all the births or miscarriages.

chunks.en: she brings a korban for the first and does not
chunks.st: Rather, she brings an offering for the first birth or miscarriage and does not bring

chunks.en: bring for the second.
chunks.st: an offering for the second miscarriage,
chunks.stMore: as it took place before the completion of the purification period for the first.

chunks.en: She brings for the third and does not
chunks.st: She then brings an offering for the third miscarriage and does not bring

chunks.en: bring for the fourth.
chunks.st: an offering for the fourth fetus,
chunks.stMore: as it was miscarried before the completion of the purification period for the third fetus.

chunks.en: These bring a korban oleh v'yored:
chunks.st: These are the five situations mentioned in the mishna (9a) in which one brings a sliding-scale offering:

chunks.en: for hearing the voice of an oath,
chunks.explain: He swore falsely that he knew no testimony.
chunks.st: For hearing the voice of an oath,
chunks.stMore: i.e., where one took a false oath that he does not have any testimony to provide on a given issue;

chunks.en: and for saying an oath with the lips,
chunks.explain: He swore falsely about something else.
chunks.st: and for the utterance of the lips,
chunks.stMore: which is a case where one took a false oath about a different matter;

chunks.en: and for making the Beis HaMikdash or its holy foods tamei,
chunks.st: and for the defiling of the Temple, by entering it while ritually impure, or defiling its sacrificial foods, by partaking of them while ritually impure;

chunks.en: and a woman who had a baby, and a metzora.
chunks.st: and a woman after childbirth; and a leper at the end of his purification process.

words.en: and the woman who had a baby

chunks.he: וּמַה בֵּין הַשִּׁפְחָה לְבֵין כָּל הָעֲרָיוֹת.
chunks.en: What is the difference between the shifchah and all the other forbidden relationships?
chunks.st: What are the differences between an espoused maidservant and all those others with whom relations are forbidden?

chunks.en: She is not the same as them, not
chunks.st: The difference is that the status of the maidservant is not equal to their status,

chunks.en: in the punishment and not in the korban.
chunks.st: neither with regard to punishment nor with regard to an offering,

chunks.en: For all the forbidden relationships one brings a chatas, but for the shifchah an asham.
chunks.st: as one who unwittingly engages in intercourse with any of those with whom relations are forbidden is liable to bring a sin offering, and by contrast, one who unwittingly engages in intercourse with an espoused maidservant is liable to bring a guilt offering.

chunks.en: For all the forbidden relationships one brings a female animal,
chunks.st: One who unwittingly engages in intercourse with any of those with whom relations are forbidden brings a female animal,

chunks.en: and for the shifchah a male.
chunks.st: and one who unwittingly engages in intercourse with an espoused maidservant brings a male animal,
chunks.stMore: as a sin offering is a female and a guilt offering is a male.

chunks.en: In all the forbidden relationships,
chunks.st: Furthermore, with regard to engaging in intercourse with any of those with whom relations are forbidden,

chunks.en: both the man and the woman
chunks.st: both the man and the woman

chunks.en: are the same for lashes and for a korban.
chunks.st: are equal with regard to liability to receive lashes if they were forewarned, and with regard to liability to bring an offering if they did so unwittingly.

chunks.he: וּבַשִּׁפְחָה לֹא הִשְׁוָה אֶת הָאִישׁ לָאִשָּׁה
chunks.en: But with the shifchah, the Torah did not make the man the same as the woman
chunks.st: And in the case of one who engages in intercourse with a maidservant, the Torah did not equate the man with the woman

chunks.he: בַּמַּכּוֹת וְלֹא אֶת הָאִשָּׁה לָאִישׁ בַּקָּרְבָּן.
chunks.en: for lashes, and not the woman the same as the man for a korban.
chunks.st: with regard to lashes, as she alone is flogged, as will be explained, and the Torah did not equate the woman with the man with regard to bringing an offering,
chunks.stMore: as she does not bring an offering.

chunks.en: In all the forbidden relationships,
chunks.st: With regard to intercourse with any of those with whom relations are forbidden,

chunks.en: the Torah counts just starting the sin like finishing it,
chunks.st: the Torah rendered the halakhic status of one who engages in the initial stage of intercourse [hame’areh] to be like that of one who completes the act,

chunks.en: and he must bring a korban for each and every time.
chunks.st: and one is liable to bring a sin offering for each and every act of intercourse that he performs unwittingly.
chunks.stMore: By contrast, in the case of relations with an espoused maidservant, one is liable only for completing the act of intercourse, and the man brings a single offering for several transgressions.

chunks.en: This is a stricter rule for the shifchah:
chunks.st: This is a stringency that the Torah imposed with regard to the maidservant relative to other individuals with whom relations are forbidden:

chunks.en: the Torah made one who did it on purpose like one who did it by mistake.
chunks.explain: Both of them bring an asham.
chunks.st: That the Torah established her status so that the one who engages in intercourse with her intentionally is like the one who does so unwittingly,
chunks.stMore: as both are liable to bring a guilt offering, whereas one who engages in intercourse with those with whom relations are forbidden is liable to bring a sin offering only when he does so unwittingly.

words.en: one who does it on purpose
like one who does it by mistake

summary: Who is the shifchah that the Torah talks about? Rabbi Akiva says she is half a maidservant and half free; Rabbi Yishmael says she is a full maidservant.

chunks.en: Who is the shifchah?
chunks.st: Who is the espoused maidservant in question?

chunks.he: כֹּל שֶׁחֶצְיָהּ שִׁפְחָה וְחֶצְיָהּ בַּת חוֹרִין,
chunks.en: Any woman who is half a maidservant and half free,
chunks.st: It is any woman who is half-maidservant half-free woman,
chunks.stMore: i.e., a maidservant who belonged to two masters, one of whom liberated her,

chunks.en: as it says (Vayikra 19),
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "and she was redeemed but not redeemed."
chunks.explain: She was set free only partly.
chunks.st: “And she was redeemed and not redeemed” (Leviticus 19:20),
chunks.stMore: which means that she was partially but not completely redeemed.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Akiva says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael says:

chunks.en: she is a full maidservant.
chunks.st: An espoused maidservant is a full-fledged maidservant whose status is certain,
chunks.stMore: as the language of the verse does not mean redeemed and not redeemed; it is simply a way of stating that she was not redeemed.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says:

chunks.en: All the forbidden relationships are written out in the Torah,
chunks.st: All those with whom relations are forbidden are enumerated in the Torah,

chunks.en: so what is left?
chunks.st: and we have

chunks.en: We only have one who is half
chunks.st: no exception other than one who is half-maidservant

chunks.en: a maidservant and half free.
chunks.st: half-free woman.

summary: In other forbidden relationships, a child, a sleeping person, or one who sinned by mistake is treated differently from the other one.
stIntro: This mishna cites an additional difference between the status of an espoused maidservant and the status of forbidden relatives.

chunks.en: In all the forbidden relationships,
chunks.st: In all cases of intercourse with those with whom relations are forbidden,

chunks.en: if one is grown up and one is a child,
chunks.st: if one is an adult and one is a minor,

chunks.en: the child is free from punishment.
chunks.st: the minor is exempt;

chunks.en: If one is awake and one is asleep,
chunks.st: if one is awake and one is sleeping,

chunks.en: the sleeping one is free.
chunks.st: the sleeping one is exempt;

chunks.en: If one did it by mistake and one on purpose,
chunks.st: if one commits the act unwittingly and one does so intentionally,

chunks.en: the one who did it by mistake brings a chatas, and the one who did it on purpose gets kares.
chunks.st: the one who did so unwittingly is liable to bring a sin offering and the one who did so intentionally is liable to be punished with karet.
chunks.stMore: By contrast, in a case of intercourse with an espoused maidservant, the man is liable to bring a guilt offering only if the woman is flogged, and that is the case only if she was an adult, awake, and committed the sin intentionally.
